correctness.rationale: Under the explicitly stated Alexandrov upper-set topology, the finite up-down path lemma gives an exact root/leaf characterization of \(\gamma(A,B)\). Structural induction proves all formulas invariant under root atomic type, support of leaf types, and point kind. Global existence \(E=\gamma(\top,-)\), root marker \(d\top\), and literal type tests define each reachable profile by a depth-two formula, so exactly \(2^N\) Boolean combinations exist. The two-valuation depth-one indistinguishability example is rigorous for every \(k\ge1,\ m\ge2\); \(E(L\land p)\) separates at depth two. Support-count summation gives saturation and exact boundary. Independently coded path reachability and coordinate tests passed for small finite cases; not represented as an infinite proof.
residual_risks: Unrestricted-parameter proof is mathematical, not an automated formal certificate.

value.rationale: The exact size and modal-depth of the whole formula algebra, for every fixed star size and every finite number of propositional variables, is a natural invariant of the newly emphasized topological reachability language. The result exposes a strict two-level expressive hierarchy, proves inability to count repeated leaf types, and identifies the exact finite-size saturation threshold \(m=2^k\). It is not a small ad hoc enumeration: arbitrary formulas and all parameters are classified with constructive representatives. This matters to finite-model checking and deciding equivalence on canonical branching Alexandrov spaces.
residual_risks: No complexity lower bound for formula-size of depth-two normal forms is asserted.
The exact invariant is specific to a finite rooted-star family and cannot be extrapolated to general finite topologies.
